account.conflictBody: The account is at revision {rev} and this browser has changes too. Pick which copy wins — nothing is overwritten until you do.
account.lockedHelp: This device is signed in but has no encryption key — enter your password to unlock it.
account.migrateBody: This browser has data and your new account has none. Upload it so your phone and desktop see the same dashboard?

account.privacyRest: it changed, not what is in it, and not your password.

account.recoverWarn: The stored copy was encrypted with the old password and will be removed — this recovers your account, not your data. Re-sync from a device that still has it.
account.recoveryBody: There is no e-mail reset on this server. If you forget your password this code lets you set a new one — but the copy stored on the server was encrypted with the old password and cannot be read afterwards, so keep this browser's data until you have re-synced.

accrual.emptyNote: No open billing period to accrue against yet.

accrual.notStartedNote: The open period starts after your newest reading — nothing has accrued yet.
accrual.paceNone: Not enough readings yet to draw a pace line.

accrual.paceRunRate: Pace = this period's own run-rate of {daily}/day — no projection is available yet.

accrual.tierCrossPace: Tier 1's {kwh} kWh runs out {day} at this pace — everything after bills at the tier-2 rate, which this line does not include.

diag.emptyDetail: It contains no bytes at all.
diag.emptyHint: Download the export again from your utility portal and retry.
diag.entityDetail: The document contains a DOCTYPE with an <!ENTITY …> declaration. External entities are a known way to read files from the machine doing the parsing, so they are refused on purpose.
diag.entityHeadline: This file declares XML external entities, which are not accepted.
diag.entityHint1: Re-export the data from your utility portal — genuine Green Button files do not define entities.
diag.entityHint2: If this file came from somewhere else, treat it as untrusted and do not open it elsewhere either.
diag.entriesDetail: Each <entry> should contain an <IntervalBlock> with <IntervalReading> elements (the actual meter readings). None were present — the export carried only metadata (usage point, meter, or summary information).
diag.entriesHeadline_one: Found {count} entry, but no interval readings inside them.
diag.entriesHeadline_other: Found {count} entries, but no interval readings inside them.
diag.entriesHint1: Choose the export option that includes interval data (hourly or 15-minute readings).
diag.entriesHint2: If the portal offers “summary” and “interval/detail” exports, pick interval/detail.
diag.htmlDetail: The file starts with HTML. Portals often hand back a login or error page when the download link expires — the Green Button export itself was never saved.
diag.htmlHeadline: That looks like a web page, not an export.
diag.htmlHint1: Sign in to your utility portal again and use the Green Button / “Download My Data” export action.
diag.htmlHint2: The file you want is usually named *.xml and starts with “<?xml” or “<feed”.
diag.malformedDetail: The file ended before its tags were balanced.
diag.malformedHeadlineLine: The XML is not well-formed at line {line}.
diag.malformedHint1: Downloads sometimes get truncated — re-download the export and try again.
diag.malformedHint2: If you edited the file by hand, restore the original.
diag.noDataDetail: The XML is readable, but it has no <entry> sections and no <IntervalReading> elements — there is no meter data in it.
diag.noDataHeadline: No Green Button data found in this file.
diag.noDataHint1: Make sure you exported “Green Button Download My Data” (XML), not a bill, summary or usage chart.
diag.noDataHint2: Some portals split the file by date range — export the full range and retry.
diag.noRowsDetail: The document has {count} entries and {readings} readings, but none of them yielded a usable timestamp/value pair.
diag.noRowsHeadline: This file looks like Green Button data but produced no readable rows.
diag.noRowsHint1: Try a different date range or a full export from your utility portal.
diag.noRowsHint2: If it keeps happening, re-download the file — this one may be truncated.
diag.noTimeDetail: Every <IntervalReading> needs a <timePeriod><start>…</start></timePeriod> holding a Unix timestamp. Without it a reading cannot be placed on the timeline, so nothing can be imported.
diag.noTimeHeadline_one: Found {count} reading, but none of them has a timestamp.
diag.noTimeHeadline_other: Found {count} readings, but none of them has a timestamp.
diag.noTimeHint1: Re-download the export — this one lost its time period block.
diag.noTimeHint2: If the file was edited or converted, use the original download.
diag.notXmlDetail: The file starts with “{head}…”, which is not the “<” an XML export begins with.
diag.notXmlHint1: Use the Green Button / “Download My Data” export from your utility portal (it produces an .xml file).
diag.notXmlHintJson: JSON exports are not supported — export XML.
diag.notXmlHintOther: CSV and PDF downloads are not supported.

ev.againstMoving: against moving the same kWh to 23:00–07:00 on Ultra-Low Overnight.
ev.alreadyOptimal: Already in the overnight window — you're optimal at this hour, nothing to shift.
ev.alreadyOvernightDiff: You already charge {label}, inside 23:00–07:00 — nothing to shift. {stay} now on {plan} vs {move} on Ultra-Low Overnight: that {delta} is the plan, not the clock.
ev.alreadyOvernightSame: You already charge {label} — inside ULO's 23:00–07:00 window, at the cheapest rate those hours ever get: {stay} now, {move} after a switch. Nothing to gain by moving this charge.
ev.assumeBand: The stay side spreads your charge across {band} — the {hour}:00 you told us, plus one hour either side for habit drift — and prices each of those hours from your own readings ({seasons} rates, weekday and weekend windows as they fell).
ev.assumeBasisHour: priced it at the {hour}:00 you told us, not at the block we found
ev.assumeCommodityOnly: Rates are OEB commodity only — delivery, regulatory charges and HST are not in these numbers.
ev.assumeDetected: Charging window read from your own data: {label}, {detail}. We can only see a block of load — we cannot tell an EV apart from any other timed appliance.
ev.assumeDoubleCount: Stay vs move prices only your charging kWh — the SAME energy the three-plan comparison credits once, below. Two views of one credit: don't add them together.
ev.assumeNoBlockBound: No overnight charging block turned up in your data, so the plan comparison prices this energy as if it charges during your most expensive hours today. Treat the swing as an upper bound, not a measurement.
ev.assumeNoBlockHour: No overnight charging block turned up in your data — the hour you gave ({hour}:00) is the only evidence of when this charge happens.
ev.assumePeakExposure: {label} is ULO On-Peak at {rate}/kWh — the exposure flagged below.
ev.assumePerCharge: $ per charge assumes the whole charge lands in 23:00–07:00, the ULO overnight window.
ev.assumeStay: The stay side prices your charge where your own data puts it ({label}), read back from the readings' period charges.
ev.assumeTagged: You tagged {tagged} kWh a night; the overnight block in your data averages {actual} kWh/night ({label}). We priced YOUR number and {basis}.
ev.assumeWorstCase: No readings at {label}, so the "stay put" side prices your charge at your plan's most expensive rate — an upper bound, not a measurement.
ev.betterOff: Staying at {label} on {plan} costs {stay}. Moving the same charge to 23:00–07:00 on Ultra-Low Overnight costs {move} — {delta} better off every month.
ev.blurb: What a night's charge costs, and what your weekday 4–9pm window is worth at risk.
ev.exposureBasis_one: Commodity only — no delivery, regulatory charges or HST. And a run-rate, not a metered month: every /month here is this window scaled to 30.4 days from {days} day of your data.
ev.exposureBasis_other: Commodity only — no delivery, regulatory charges or HST. And a run-rate, not a metered month: every /month here is this window scaled to 30.4 days from {days} days of your data.
ev.headlineLead: A night's charge on ULO costs
ev.hourPrefilled: Charging hour prefilled from the block we found ({label}).
ev.noBlock: We could not find an overnight charging block in your data — type yours and we will price it.
ev.notReady: Tag a nightly kWh above to price the charge under all three plans.
ev.ofThat: Of that: {shift}/mo for moving the hour, {plan}/mo for changing plan at your hour. The two add up to the total and are never counted twice.
ev.peakExposureBody_one: {count} weekday afternoon hour sits in ULO's 16:00–21:00 peak window. Keep using it and a ULO switch makes it one of the most expensive hours you buy.
ev.peakExposureBody_other: {count} weekday afternoon hours sit in ULO's 16:00–21:00 peak window. Keep using them and a ULO switch makes them the most expensive hours you buy.

ev.pickHour: Pick the hour your car draws the most power and we will price staying there against moving to midnight.
ev.priceAtHour: above — we will price staying at that hour on

ev.stayDetailUpper: No readings at {label}, so the stay side is priced at each plan's most expensive rate — an upper bound, not a measurement.

gbseries.none: no billable readings — this point's data could not be priced
gbseries.reasons: Why some of this point was left out:
heatmap.blurb: Weekdays and weekends split apart — a charger that only runs Monday to Friday at 19:00 disappears when Saturday and Sunday share its colour scale. Both grids use the SAME scale (peaking at {max} in an hour), so the colours stay comparable.

hindsight.behaviourChipFlat: BEHAVIOUR · FLAT RATE — THE HOUR DOESN'T CHANGE THE PRICE
hindsight.behaviourLever: Behaviour lever · load that never moved
hindsight.behaviourUnknownNote: Without a known plan there is no rate to move a block into, so the behaviour side is left out rather than guessed.
hindsight.behaviourUntrustedNote: Shown for information only — the model cannot reproduce this bill, so these block costs stay out of every total.
hindsight.blurb: Per closed bill: the plan you were on against the cheapest one, and the load you ran in an expensive window that could have run in a cheap one. Modelled, labelled, and never a claim about what you would have done.
hindsight.eyebrow: What should have happened · every closed period
hindsight.flatRateNote: Tiered prices every hour the same and a same-day shift never changes the month's volume, so moving a block here saves exactly $0. The plan is the only lever on this period.
hindsight.headlineEmpty: Nothing auditable yet — this file holds {total} periods, and a period needs a known plan type plus readings covering {coverage}% of it before either lever can be priced.
hindsight.legendCounterfactual: Behaviour is a counterfactual: IF the named block had run in the named cheap window instead, this period would have cost that much less. Same readings, same plan, same rate set — only the hours change. Each block is priced on its own, so the total is what all of them together were worth, not a claim that they all happened.
hindsight.legendMeta: {periods} periods · {plan} counted on the plan lever · {behaviour} counted on the behaviour lever · {kwh} kWh ran inside a recurring block.
hindsight.legendPlanSide: The plan alternatives and the $1 model check come from the audited switch track record above — this panel reads those numbers, it does not re-price them.
hindsight.leverBehaviour: Behaviour was the bigger lever — {behaviour} was left on the table by not moving load, against {plan} from the plan you were on.
hindsight.leverNeither: Neither lever had real money on it: the plan you were on was already the cheapest, and no recurring load could have moved.
hindsight.leverPlan: Plan was the bigger lever — staying put cost {plan} against {behaviour} left on the table by not moving load.
hindsight.leverUnknown: One of the two levers cannot be measured on this data, so they are not compared.
hindsight.moveEvidence: seen {weeks} of {of} weeks · volume steady within {cv} · {confidence}
hindsight.noteEmpty: Import a bill history to see what every closed period should have cost.
hindsight.noteNothingCountable: None of the {total} periods in this file can be audited yet — a period needs a known plan type and readings that cover it before either lever can be priced.
hindsight.noteReady: Across {periods} periods: {plan} of over-payment from the plan you were on, {behaviour} from load that never moved.
hindsight.nothingToShiftNote: No block of hours recurred often enough and steadily enough inside this period to be called a routine — nothing was moveable.
hindsight.planLeverSaved: Plan lever · the alternatives would have cost more
hindsight.planUnknownNote: The bill's own lines fingerprint no plan and no entry in your timeline covers this period — nothing is claimed on either lever.
hindsight.title: Hindsight
hindsight.tooFewWeeksNote_one: This period spans {weeks} week — too few to call any block of hours a routine, so nothing is claimed.
hindsight.tooFewWeeksNote_other: This period spans {weeks} weeks — too few to call any block of hours a routine, so nothing is claimed.
hindsight.totalNote: The two levers are disjoint — this sum is the plan miss plus the behaviour miss, never a single "you could have saved" figure.
